review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the simp lemmas in Archimedean/Class.lean (mk_one, mk_eq_top_iff, mk_eq_mk) and grepped for uses of the `*_nonneg` lemmas. I found no competing rules or rewrite cycles. The `mk_mul`, `mk_pow`, `mk_zpow`, `mk_inv` and `mk_div` rewrites all go from ring expressions to class expressions and look terminating and confluent. The `mk_intCast`, `mk_natCast`, `mk_ofNat` and `mk_ratCast` lemmas are conditional simp lemmas whose side conditions simp can discharge. The one finding is mild: `0 ≤ mk (f y)` is not a simp lemma, so the file's own proof has to pass it to `simp` by hand. I did not run Lean, so I cannot say whether the suggested attribute would cause any simp-set problem.

findings.excerpt: theorem mk_map_nonneg_of_archimedean [Archimedean S] (f : S →+*o R) (y : S) : 0 ≤ mk (f y) := by
findings.problem: The unconditional fact `0 ≤ mk (f y)` for a ring hom `f` out of an archimedean ring is not tagged `@[simp]`. The file's own downstream proof, `mk_nonneg_of_le_of_le_of_archimedean`, has to pass it to `simp` by hand. Its sibling cast lemmas (`mk_intCast_nonneg`, `mk_natCast_nonneg`, `mk_ratCast_nonneg`) are not simp either. They cover exactly the cases the simp lemmas `mk_intCast`, `mk_natCast` and `mk_ratCast` leave open, where the cast might be 0. So `simp` can prove `mk (n : S) = 0` when `n ≠ 0` is known, but it cannot prove `0 ≤ mk (n : S)` for an arbitrary `n`.
findings.proposed_change: Consider tagging `mk_map_nonneg_of_archimedean` with `@[simp]`, since its LHS `0 ≤ mk (f y)` is a unification-friendly pattern that does not change under simp. Then drop the explicit argument in `simp [mk_map_nonneg_of_archimedean]` at line 237. Consider the same for `mk_intCast_nonneg`, `mk_natCast_nonneg` and `mk_ratCast_nonneg`, after checking that they do not interfere with the conditional `mk_intCast`, `mk_natCast` and `mk_ratCast` rewrites. Those three have unconstrained `n` or `q`, so they only fire on `0 ≤ mk _` goals.
findings.benefit: Callers would get `0 ≤ mk (f y)` and `0 ≤ mk (n : S)` from plain `simp`. Today the StandardPart file has to name `mk_map_nonneg_of_archimedean` explicitly in each use, and the file's own proof at line 237 does the same.
